newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-LEICESTERSHIRE SET TO WIN TITLE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LEICESTERSHIRE SET TO WIN TITLE.

text.p: Leicestershire can secure the English County Championship crown without winning their final match after Surrey were thwarted in their penultimate game on Monday.

Kent stayed on the title trail with a remarkable 148-run over Hampshire, but Surrey and Essex both failed to push their claims. Surrey were held to a draw at Cardiff while Essex virtually dropped out of contention after losing to Sussex.

Leicestershire, who wrapped up a two-day victory over Durham last Friday, moved 14 points ahead of second-placed Surrey, with Kent a further point adrift. Essex, the only other team theoretically capable of overhauling the leaders, stood 23 points behind.
If Leicestershire earn maximum bonus points from their final game against Middlesex, starting at Leicester on Thursday, a draw will be enough to give them the title.
Surrey's hopes of lifting the championship for the first time in 25 years were doused by Glamorgan in Cardiff.
Set the unlikely task of scoring 336 to win off what turned out to be 51 overs, Surrey finished on 205 for seven.
When Matthew Maynard declared the Glamorgan second innings at 442 for nine, Alec Stewart shuffled his batting order, sending in Brendon Julian to open.

Surrey slumped to 15 for two, then Chris Lewis plundered 40 runs off just 28 deliveries and Adam Hollioake struck three sixes and eight fours in reaching 85 off 70 balls. But, when he was bowled by Robert Croft with the total on 154 for five, the struggle for victory became a battle for survival.
Kent stayed in the hunt with a remarkable 148-run win over Hampshire at Canterbury, where the visitors lost their last eight wickets in just 44 balls.
Hampshire collapsed from 143 for one to 150 all out as Martin McCague took five for three in 17 deliveries, including his first hat-trick for the county.
It was Kent's second hat-trick of the match following Dean Headley's record-equalling third triple of the season on Saturday.
McCague finished with figures of six for 51 and he and Headley have now taken more than 100 championship wickets between them this season.
Ian Salisbury returned career-best figures of eight for 75 as Sussex claimed a 137-run victory over Essex at Chelmsford.
Faced with a daunting victory target of 421, Essex were bowled out for 283 as leg-spinner Salisbury found some help from the pitch, and exploited it in style.
